correctness.rationale: For commutative unital rings, prime-graph adjacency is exactly zero product. The zero vertex makes every nonedge a distance-two pair. The number of ordered zero-product pairs is the exact gcd sum \(\sum_x\gcd(x,n)\), which factors as \(\prod p^{a-1}((a+1)p-a)\). Removing the diagonal square-zero solutions \(\prod p^{\lfloor a/2\rfloor}\) and halving gives the edge count. Direct substitution then yields the Hosoya and Wiener formulas. The derivation handles all primes and exponent boundaries, including \(a=1\).

originality.rationale: The 2024 primary paper gives only the cases \(p,p^2,p^3,pq,p^2q,p^2q^2,pqr\) and explicitly lists four broader families as open. The displayed product formula covers arbitrary prime factorizations and therefore strictly dominates those cases. published-finding corpus and web searches for the all-\(n\) formula, divisor-sum form, gcd-sum form, and zero-product aliases found no matching published result. A 2025 prime-graph paper treats diameter/girth rather than Wiener index.
residual_risks: An equivalent counting formula may exist under a different graph name and may not be indexed by prime-graph terminology.

The universal finite-ring annihilator-sum identity is elementary; novelty is claimed for its explicit all-n specialization to the named prime-graph Wiener problem, not for the abstract counting tautology by itself.

value.rationale: The result replaces a growing list of case-by-case distance-matrix formulas by one closed multiplicative expression for every Z_n. It directly answers all four open families stated in the 2024 primary source, includes the entire distance distribution via the Hosoya polynomial, and provides a short reusable counting mechanism rather than a one-off numerical extension.
